heuristics.name: shared-function-random-mapping
heuristics.statement: One fixed r=64 r-adding walk function with a uniform table and wrapping residues from P uniform starts matches uniform random sampling with the 63/64 distinct-partition merge factor for the birthday bound, merged-suffix tail steps sample distinguished points at density 2^-32, and a solved collision is degenerate with probability 1/q.
heuristics.support: Standard-regime construction matching Teske's analyzed r-adding walks (r=64, uniform table, wrapping residues by the lazy-reduction lemma, uniform starts) with van Oorschot-Wiener parallel distinguished points; reproduced Teske+Harris analysis in proof.md; record computations confirm predictions at scale; degeneracy quantified at 1/q. Toy experiments confirm merging and recovery end to end.

heuristics.name: salted-hash-bucket-independence
heuristics.statement: Independent uniform salts give independent uniform bucket assignments on the fixed key set.
heuristics.support: Precise salted-hash heuristic with fully specified splitmix64 absorption in proof.md; the bound is over salt randomness and needing a second re-salt requires two independently bad salts (2^-514 chain-rule event).

limitations: Analytic construction; no full-size execution or independent qualification.
Success relies on the supported multi-walk random-mapping heuristic.
Instruction budgets are conservative analytic upper bounds, not measured assembly.
The 2^98-entry table is an analytic device, as is the baseline's larger table.
Beats the generic BSGS control via batched parallel rho at the 0.39 threshold; not novel cryptanalysis.
Supersedes v8: standard-regime wrapping coefficients with lazy reduction, quantified 1/q degeneracy, salt-framed fully specified hash, exact ceil-step/start charging.
